clue.text: News of lentil soup, for example — nice to cook

indicators.note: in a soup things are stirred together into a mush, so the word before it is mixed up
cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the word before it is reworked too

parts.note: taken as written
EG is the usual abbreviation for 'for example'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe note: lentil soup is an example of something nice to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces, LENTIL, EG and NICE, go into one pot and are shuffled together to make INTELLIGENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in its older sense means information or tidings received, as in military intelligence.

clue.text: Very large fellows with semi-organised exterior

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters of semi are rearranged
an exterior is an outer layer, so the rearranged letters wrap around the fellows

parts.note: the letters of semi, rearranged and split around the middle piece
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Some enormous chaps are only half-heartedly organised on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-organised' reads as one word meaning partly tidy, but the hyphen hides a split: semi is the fodder and organised the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense is a straightforward synonym meaning huge or vast in size.

clue.text: Victim of 7, old ship with title docked first

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter
first says this shortened word comes at the front, before the vessel

parts.note: title with its final letter cut off
Noah's ark is the famous old ship

explanation.surface: An old vessel carrying a shortened title painted at its bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is KILL TWO BIRDS, so a victim of 7 is any bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A titlark is an old name for the pipit, a small songbird, so it is one of the birds that might be killed.

clue.text: Dot's follower among the ransacked went by train?

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the follower goes inside the other word

parts.note: what is ransacked has been looted
in a web address, dot is followed by com

explanation.surface: A tale of a Morse dot, or a follower named Dot, mixed up with plundered goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' suggests Morse code or a woman's name, but think of web addresses: dot-com.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomoted means moved from place to place; the question mark admits the pun on a locomotive, which pulls a train.

clue.text: Something put in to rinse the clothes

indicators.note: clothes is used as a verb meaning covers, so the outer words wrap round the hidden one

parts.note: the run of letters inside rinse the

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions: add something to the wash to rinse the clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like the laundry being washed, but it is a verb: the words rinse the clothe, that is cover, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a piece inserted into something else, such as a panel in a dress or a small map within a larger one.

clue.text: Cut up politician on the French pattern

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
MP is a Member of Parliament
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A politician is cut up by someone following the French model.
explanation.definitionFit: An example can be a model or pattern to be copied, as in setting a good example.

clue.text: Drawing goes round on the wagon to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the vehicle comes at the very start, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a cart is a wagon
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sketch is passed around among teetotallers, people 'on the wagon'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' looks like the idiom for giving up drink, but the words split apart, and 'to begin with' puts the wagon at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a humorous drawing, or a preparatory sketch for a painting.

clue.text: Economise on performance — bag a brace (1 across by candid person)

indicators.note: by means beside, so the second part of the phrase sits next to the first

parts.note: to bag game is to kill it, and a brace is a pair of shot birds
1 across is intelligence, and wit is intelligence
a candid person is an honest one

explanation.surface: A thrifty sportsman bags a pair of birds, with a note from the gossip columns.
explanation.walkthrough: WIT plus HONEST ONE runs together as WITH ONE STONE. 7 is the theme: the bird answers are its victims.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means achieving two aims with a single action, which saves effort, so it is economising on performance.

clue.text: Faddish, in theory, like a sort of compass without leaders

indicators.note: without leaders means the front letters are taken away

parts.note: a prismatic compass is a surveyor's compass with a prism for sighting

explanation.surface: A compass that has lost its guiding lights is following the latest fashion in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the two leading letters, PR, from PRISMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ismatic describes devotion to isms, that is fashionable doctrines or theories, so it means faddish in matters of theory.

clue.text: Victims of 7 fight and fight with Howard in cinema

parts.note: to spar is to fight
a row is a fight or quarrel
Howard Hawks was a Hollywood film director

explanation.surface: A brawl at the pictures involving someone called Howard.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard Hawks directed films such as The Big Sleep and Rio Bravo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrowhawks are small birds of prey, and any birds are the victims of killing two birds with one stone.

clue.text: See 7
The power of the law, at a stretch?

parts.note: surface reading: the reach of the police and courts
setter's reading: a limb fully stretched out is at its greatest length

explanation.walkthrough: 'At a stretch' sounds like 'just about', but it pictures a limb extended to full reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the long arm of the law' means the far-reaching authority of the police to catch offenders.

clue.text: Supplier of nourishment put by an expert into a child

indicators.note: put together with into says one piece is placed inside another
into means going inside, so the expert goes inside the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a pro is an expert, with the a taken as written

explanation.surface: An expert puts food into a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproot is a plant's main root growing straight down, which draws up water and nutrients.

clue.text: Something to do with vengeance reportedly causes a stink

definitions.note: the answer is the verb you do with vengeance

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the answer matches the spoken sound of the next words

parts.note: to reek is to smell strongly

explanation.surface: A smelly act of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The W is silent, so the two words are spoken the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Vengeance is wreaked: wreak means inflict, and that verb is almost always paired with revenge or havoc.

clue.text: Thus far the little pig is without errors and omissions

indicators.note: is without means stands outside, so the pig wraps round the first error

parts.note: the runt is the smallest pig of a litter
E as in E&OE, errors and omissions excepted
O as in E&OE, errors and omissions excepted

explanation.surface: So far, the runt of the litter has made no mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: E&OE, errors and omissions excepted, is printed on invoices. E goes inside THE RUNT, and O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is an old legal adverb meaning up to that point or to that thing.

clue.text: Victims of 7 for 5, so we all dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: 5 down is example, and 'for example' abbreviates to EG
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd breaking up after some example has been given.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle owls are very large owls, and any birds are the victims of killing two birds with one stone.

clue.text: Awfully odd beggar, like victim of 7, but beasts

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the following letters are put in a disordered arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange tramp likened to a pair of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird answers each join two birds, as in sparrow and hawk; this one joins two beasts in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger-dog is a dachshund, and its name is two animal names fused together, like the compound bird names.

clue.text: Such as this comic hero died — and live

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
taken as written
to live is to be, and are is a form of be

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero who dies and comes back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare, Pilot of the Future, was the space hero of the British boys' comic the Eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan Dare is a famous British comic-strip character, the square-jawed spaceman of the 1950s.

clue.text: If it's up to me, I have to be bringing tears to eyes, etc

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone saying that, if the decision were theirs, they would be moving everyone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's up to me' reads as 'my decision', but up is the reversal of 'to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means arousing strong feeling, and tears are the typical sign of a stirred emotion.

clue.text: Flying beast, male, to swim?

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Asking whether a male bat can swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe can mean to go swimming, especially in the sea, in British usage.

clue.text: Straightway the old priest is put in the old well

indicators.note: is put in means placed inside, so the priest goes within the other word

parts.note: bene is Latin for well, an old language
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric is lowered into an ancient well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straightway' looks like the old adverb meaning immediately; read as two words, straight way, it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the most direct route, the straight course a bee is supposed to fly home.

clue.text: "Mother's ruin" is taken for drinking

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer: a flask taken along for drinks

indicators.note: ruin means wreck, so the letters before it are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Gin, 'mother's ruin', is being drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is a set phrase for gin, which tempts the solver to think of drink; here ruin simply wrecks the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask carried on outings to keep drinks hot or cold.

clue.text: Place for cattle with no entry to loch

indicators.note: an entry is a way in, so the word goes inside the other

parts.note: a ranch is a cattle farm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cattle farm with no access to the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no entry' reads as 'barred', but it means with NO entering.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Rannoch is a long freshwater lake in the Scottish Highlands, beside Rannoch Moor.

clue.text: See 9
The first lady and the others at the top

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Eve and everyone else standing on a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the first woman of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, the world's highest mountain, is used figuratively for the highest point or peak of anything.

clue.text: Wild waves — that is our prospect

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
'that is' abbreviates to IE, id est; the word is is shared with the link

explanation.surface: Looking out of a seaside hotel at stormy waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' gives IE, and the shuffle covers WAVES and IE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a view of a landscape, and a coastal one looking out over water is a sea view.

clue.text: Point to paid assassin succeeding where Disney succeeded

definitions.note: the answer is the surname that comes after Walt

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the assassin follows the point

parts.note: W is west, a compass point
a hitman is a contract killer

explanation.surface: A Hollywood thriller about a hired killer achieving success.
explanation.walkthrough: Disney's first name is Walt; Whitman comes after Walt in the name of the poet, which is where Disney is succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman was the American poet of Leaves of Grass, sharing the forename Walt with Disney.

clue.text: White cliffs of the South, which is at the heart of trained horses

indicators.note: at the heart of means in the middle, so these letters go inside the horses

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
eventers are horses trained for three-day eventing
refers back to the south, so its letter appears again
taken as written

explanation.surface: The chalk cliffs of southern England, sitting among horses in training.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Araucaria parse: 'which' points back to the South, so its letter is used twice, once at the start and once in the middle. Eventers compete in horse trials.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Sisters are a row of chalk sea cliffs on the Sussex coast of southern England.
